findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_quote_callback" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use ONLY when the person asked to get a car-insurance quote or to be contacted: creates a call-back request so that ז.א שיווק ומכירות דיגיטליים בע"מ calls them …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, lookup_vehicle, list_makes · Private data: theft_by_model, explain_licence_fee, request_quote_callback · Public sink: model_info.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, lookup_vehicle, list_makes · Private data: theft_by_model, explain_licence_fee, request_quote_callback · Public sink: model_info

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
